data.title: Unit 9: Heat, light and sound
Heat and light
data.heading: Echo
data.text: When the same sound is heard more than once, it is called an echo.
Echoes occur when sound waves are reflected or bounced back from a surface.
Echoes are clearer when sound waves bounce off hard, smooth, and flat surfaces.
An echo isn't produced when sound waves hit a soft surface.
The distance between the source of the sound and the surface the sound waves hit affect the quality of an echo.
If the distance between the source of the sound and the surface is very short, an echo won't be produced.
Please show complete bodies, not just the ear and hands.
